title: SYSK Selects: How Monopoly Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2014 episode on the history and rules of Monopoly. Josh introduces the episode as a classic pick. The hosts trace the game to Lizzie Magie's 1904 Landlord's Game, its Georgist and Quaker influences, and Ruth Hoskins and the Rayford circle who spread it, then Charles Darrow's sale of the game to Parker Brothers. They cover Monopoly's board, tokens, cards, and property layout, and modern versions. They explain the rules (buying, auctions, monopolies, houses and hotels, mortgages, jail, free parking) and strategy tips (utilities, Boardwalk and Park Place, orange properties, three-house limit). They discuss Ralph Anspach's anti-Monopoly game and the Parker Brothers lawsuit that followed. The episode ends with a rapid-fire round of listener Facebook questions.

segments.title: Intro and Mr. Monopoly banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects episode as a classic 2014 show on Monopoly. The hosts joke about Mr. Monopoly's name (Rich Uncle Pennybags) and note that the game's history has more supplemental material than most topics.

segments.title: Lizzie Magie and the Landlord's Game origins
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Landlord's Game created by Lizzie Magie, who designed it to illustrate the evils of land monopolies. It had two rule sets, one where the community benefited. It was rooted in Henry George's Georgism and was popular in socialist circles on the East Coast. Quaker friends contributed rules like fixed property prices and household-object tokens. Magie patented the game but Parker Brothers rejected her pitch.

segments.title: Ruth Hoskins, Rayford circle, and Charles Darrow
segments.summary: Ruth Hoskins and Quaker friends Jessie and Eugene Rayford in the Philadelphia and Atlantic City area changed rules toward the modern game. The game passed to Todd and then to Charles Darrow, a Depression-era salesman, who sold it to Parker Brothers. The hosts describe how Parker Brothers bought the game from Darrow and also bought Magie's patent.

segments.title: Atlantic City board and property names
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the board mirrors Atlantic City geography and the neighborhoods of the day, the Reading Railroad route between Philly and Atlantic City, and the misspelled Marvin Gardens. They also note the game's many licensed and regional versions.

segments.title: Monopoly versions and Forbes fictional rich list
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the many licensed Monopoly editions, including Star Wars, Simpsons, and the corporate version, and a custom board option. They then riff on Forbes' list of wealthiest fictional characters.

segments.title: Board pieces, tokens, and cards
segments.summary: The hosts list the Monopoly tokens, including the iron, the cat that replaced the iron in 2013, the thimble, the cannon and battleship from the failed Conflict game, and retired pieces like the horse and rider. They describe the board, the 40 squares, the properties, the cards, houses, hotels, and play money.

segments.title: Monopoly rules: buying, auctions, monopolies, and mortgages
segments.summary: The hosts walk through setup, starting with the Go square and salary, buying and auctioning properties, forming monopolies that allow double rent, building houses and hotels, mortgaging properties, and house rules like personal loans and Free Parking jackpots.

segments.title: Jail rules and strategy tips
segments.summary: The hosts explain the ways to go to jail and get out, including doubles and fifty-dollar payment, and a jail strategy. They then cover strategy advice: buy everything, cap houses at three, avoid utilities and Boardwalk and Park Place, and note that the orange properties get landed on most often.

segments.title: Anti-Monopoly and Ralph Anspach lawsuit
segments.summary: The hosts describe economist Ralph Anspach's anti-Monopoly game from the 1970s, which was designed to break up monopolies. Parker Brothers sent a cease and desist letter and sued. Anspach uncovered the game's origins and won the right to the name at the Supreme Court. His book and the later anti-Monopoly Too edition are mentioned.

segments.title: Monopoly strategy beyond the rules and wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts discuss that strategy depends on the players' personalities and cite the Monopoly World Championship. They end the main topic with a pointer to the HowStuffWorks article on Monopoly rules.

segments.title: Facebook questions rapid fire
segments.summary: The hosts answer listener questions from Facebook on topics including favorite episodes, vacuum cleaners, marriage advice, pet goats, Simpsons episodes, favorite childhood books, and the best Schwarzenegger or Stallone movie. Their sign-off closes the episode.
